scoring_status: All items are non-scoring evidence. Only scoring_rules.json defines independently scored final conclusions.

items.statement: Evidence for NPCZCS S1 spatial character
items.expected: Actual state-resolved transition density, NTOs or physically equivalent electronic evidence for NPCZCS S1 establishes hole density mainly on the carbazole–cyanostilbene framework and particle density mainly on the appended naphthalimide, supporting intramolecular charge transfer. Ground-state HOMO/LUMO images or a root label alone are insufficient. No fixed fragment partition, software, centroid cutoff or NTO weight is required.

items.statement: Evidence for NPCZCS low versus bright absorption structure
items.expected: Actual NPCZCS transition energies and intensities distinguish its S1 from a stronger higher-energy absorption transition, source S2 near 375.88 nm. S1 oscillator strength 0.4988 is contextual, not a numerical target. Establish the same-state assignment and the higher-state greater intensity from actual transition evidence; merely calling the largest band S1 does not pass. Source higher-root indices are identifiers, not immutable labels across methods; use transition character and intensity correspondence, not wavelength proximity alone.

items.statement: Evidence for Phenanthraquinone-local low-energy singlet character
items.expected: State-resolved transition-density/NTO or equivalent evidence establishes a predominantly phenanthraquinone-local low-energy singlet excitation of PQCZCS, with both hole and particle mainly on that fragment rather than donor-to-acceptor ICT. The source identifies this as S1; source S2 lies only0.0163 eV higher. If a justified method interchanges the two low roots, character correspondence within that low-energy pair can establish this character finding while explicitly reporting the changed ordering. A root label, ground-state frontier picture, arbitrary higher state or unresolved assignment alone fails. The lowest-energy comparison must still use the actual lowest root; the character mapping does not redefine S1.

items.statement: Evidence for Final acceptor-dependent molecular absorption explanation
items.expected: Compare the three physically assigned lowest singlet energies under matched conditions and explain the acceptor-dependent onset relative to the dominant bright bands. The source-compatible low-energy order is PQCZCS below AQCZCS below NPCZCS; the actual energy differences, uncertainty and transition correspondence must support the claimed ordering. Connect the larger changes of the low onset and the different spatial character (NP/AQ donor-framework-to-acceptor ICT, PQ predominantly phenanthraquinone-local) with the much closer higher bright-band energies. Thus a common donor-acceptor drawing does not imply one universal ICT spectrum. Near-degenerate PQ roots may reorder when the actual low pair and its character are tracked. An evidenced model-sensitive limitation may qualify an unresolved adjacent order, but a copied rank, missing energies, arbitrary root switching or universal ICT assertion fails. No source energy window or solid-state emission conclusion is imposed.
